decision: How should the USD-folder writer stop writing stage B using a loss report that was built for stage A?

constraints.principle_1: An export is a translation: no writer runs before its loss report exists, and a blocking report writes nothing.
constraints.one_traversal: The exporter deliberately gathers facts once (api.gather) so the census and the export read the same facts.
constraints.contract_4_4: The Writer contract is write(stage, inv, out_dir, settings); the report is supplied on the writer.

evidence: api.py builds the report and skips write() when any item blocks, so the shipping path never mismatches.
write() returns early when the supplied report blocks, but it only re-checks plan problems; census findings such as composition errors or MaterialX without UVs are not recomputed.
UsdFolderWriter(report=<GO report from stage A>).write(stage_B, ...) would write stage B even if B's own findings block.
The wave 1 adversarial review recorded this as a minor finding against principle 1.

options.recompute_in_write: Always recompute the blocking findings inside write() before writing anything, so the writer can never trust a stale report.
options.bind_identifier: Record the root layer identifier the report was built from and raise in write() when the stage it is given has a different one.

checks.stale_report_reachable: Does the evidence show a reachable path where a writer receives a report built from a different stage?
